records.outcome: a dedicated public client app for local mode exists in Microsoft Entra with a loopback redirect URI, public client flows allowed, and admin-consented delegated Graph scopes, and its client and tenant IDs are noted
preconditions: do not reuse the desktop client app registered for the remote connector
steps: In Entra admin center go to App registrations > New registration
Set Name and set Supported account types to accounts in this organizational directory only
Under Authentication open Redirect URI configuration and select Add redirect URI
Choose the Mobile and desktop applications card (Windows, UWP, Console)
Leave suggested URIs unchecked, enter http://localhost in Custom redirect URIs, and select Configure
For brokered sign-in on managed devices, add the per-platform broker redirect URI to the same platform via Edit, then Save
Set Allow public client flows to Yes and select Save
Under API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > Delegated permissions, add the scopes the connector will request
Select Grant admin consent for your organization
Note the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID from the overview page

evidence.quote: Note the **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID** from the overview page.

records.notes: Admin stage of the local-connector path; the user still signs in afterwards. A Conditional Access policy blocking device-code flow is recommended, scoped to All resources.

records.outcome: the built-in Microsoft 365 local connector is configured in Claude Desktop with the tenant and client IDs, its connection tested, and saved
preconditions: the local-mode app registration from step 1, with its Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID
steps: Open the Claude Desktop in-app configuration window
Open Connectors and select Add server
Choose Microsoft 365 under the Built-in group
Enter the Tenant ID and the Client ID from step 1
Choose the Azure cloud (global, us-gov-high, or us-gov-dod)
Leave Access empty for standard read access, or list scopes explicitly
Select Test connection to verify the server starts and lists its tools
Select Save

evidence.quote: open **Connectors**, select **Add server**, and choose **Microsoft 365** under the **Built-in** group.

records.notes: The server ships inside the app; it activates only from managed configuration and users cannot add it themselves.

records.outcome: the Microsoft 365 local connector is declared as a managedMcpServers entry in the JSON or plist configuration and deployed to devices
preconditions: configuration managed through JSON or a plist directly
the local-mode app registration from step 1
steps: Open the managed JSON or plist configuration
Add a managedMcpServers entry with the server field set to microsoft365
Set name, clientId, and tenantId
Optionally set azureCloud, continuousAccessEvaluation, scope, and toolPolicy
Deploy the configuration through your device-management tool

records.outcome: the local connector requests exactly the listed delegated Graph scopes at the next sign-in, changing which read and search tools are exposed to users
preconditions: whatever is listed must also be consented on the app registration from step 1
steps: List the delegated scopes you want in the entry's scope field
Add any of the optional read scopes needed for the extra tools
Consent the same scopes on the app registration in Entra and keep the two lists in sync

evidence.quote: To request a different set, list scopes in the entry's `scope` field.

records.notes: User.Read and offline_access are always included. An unrecognized scope name rejects the whole entry at configuration load and the connector does not appear.

records.outcome: the write tools matching the granted scopes appear on the local connector so Claude can act in Microsoft 365, each still requiring user approval on every call
preconditions: Claude Desktop 1.19367.0 or later; 1.24012.0 or later for the Teams write tools
steps: Add the desired write scopes to the entry's scope field
Consent the same write scopes on the app registration from step 1
Optionally adjust per-tool approval with toolPolicy, noting that allow resolves to ask for the send tools

evidence.quote: grant write scopes: add them to the entry's `scope` field and consent them on the app registration from step 1

records.notes: Granting a subset of the write scopes exposes a matching subset of the tools; removing them returns the connector to read-only.

records.outcome: the previously granted consent is removed in Entra, so tokens carrying those scopes can no longer be obtained for the app
preconditions: Microsoft Entra admin access to the local-mode app registration
steps: In Entra open Enterprise applications and select your app
Open Permissions
Remove the consent

evidence.quote: To revoke access, remove the consent in Entra under **Enterprise applications → your app → Permissions**.

records.notes: Narrowing or removing the scope field alone does not narrow tokens already obtainable for the registration.
